Final task of the architecture campaign (PRs #9194–#9209): add automated regression protection for the highest-value architectural invariants. **Tests + architecture metadata only — no production code changed.**

items.title: fix: correct XP formula power function
items.body:
## Summary

Fix a critical bug in the XP level progression formula and add comprehensive tests.

## Root Cause

The `_pow()` function in `PlayerProfileModel` was incorrectly implemented - it just returned the base value instead of computing `base^exponent`. This caused the XP level progression formula to return incorrect values.

**Before:**
```dart
static double _pow(int base, double exponent) {
  return base.toDouble();  // Wrong!
}
```

**After:**
```dart
static double _pow(int base, double exponent) {
  return math.pow(base, exponent).toDouble();  // Correct
}
```

## Changes

1. **Bug Fix**: `lib/models/models.dart` - Import `dart:math` and use proper `math.pow()` function
2. **Tests**: `test/models_test.dart` - Add comprehensive tests for `xpForLevel`:
   - Test XP calculation for multiple levels (1, 2, 3, 5, 10)
   - Test handling of levels < 1
   - Test `xpRequiredForLevel` helper function

## Impact

The XP formula `250 × level^1.5 + 500` was returning `250 × level + 500` instead, causing incorrect XP requirements for leveling up. This affected the entire gamification system.

## Test Plan

- [x] CI tests pass (46 tests)
- [x] All analyze checks pass
- [x] XP level progression works correctly

## Additional Fixes

- Updated README to reflect actual Flutter version (3.22.0)
- Updated XP formula documentation to match actual implementation

items.title: fix: only dedupe secrets issues [IDE-2140]
items.body:
### Description

Secrets issues are classed as "one or more instances of a secret in a file". Other scan types treat each instance as an individual issue.

Our deduplication code was incorrectly collapsing some non-secrets issues down (e.g., credentials picked up by the Code scanner, or repeated strings containing issues). 

This fix only collapses on the issue fingerprint if it is a Secrets issue, else it uses the unique identifiers of the issues to count instances.

I've not checked this in, but I did write a test to verify this using a real customer dataset that was incorrectly being deduplicated, and have confirmed that the fix gives the correct totals.

items.title: Fix iOS/Android audio delay and improve sound layering
items.body:
On iOS Safari, `AudioContext` is suspended at page load and can only be resumed on a user gesture. The previous code called `audioCtx.resume()` inside `playSound()` - but since `resume()` is async, the first sound after a gesture was delayed by 50–200ms. iOS also re-suspends audio after phone calls, Siri, or app switching, and there was no recovery for that.

Additionally, `playSound` always stopped any existing instance before playing, so rapid collisions (bricks, bullets) would cut each other off instead of overlapping.

**Changes**

- **`_unlockAudio()`** - one-shot listener on `touchstart`/`pointerdown`/`mousedown`/`keydown` that calls `audioCtx.resume()` and plays a silent 1-sample buffer to warm the iOS audio graph, then removes itself
- **`visibilitychange` + `focus` listeners** - resume `AudioContext` when the page regains visibility, covering iOS interruptions
- **`playSound` reworked** - short SFX now allow up to 3 overlapping instances; the 4th evicts the oldest. Pass `{ loop: true }` or `{ restart: true }` to get the old single-instance behaviour. Fallback `resume()` kept as a safety net
- **README** updated - the previous description ("calling playSound twice restarts it") was incorrect for SFX; now correctly describes the overlap-up-to-3 behaviour
- **Sound tests expanded** - 4 new behavioural tests covering rapid play, cap eviction, loop restart, and stop after multiple plays

items.title: fix(poly-g): trim R2's 3' poly-G tail (was incorrectly 5' poly-C)
items.body:
## Summary

Fix for [#321](https://github.com/FelixKrueger/TrimGalore/issues/321) (reported by @K81ta).

The 2-colour poly-G artifact is **sequencer-induced** (the instrument calls "no signal" as a high-quality G when it overruns the template), and it manifests at the **3' end of every read regardless of strand orientation**. The original code copied the poly-A `revcomp = is_r2` cross-strand pattern — correct for poly-A (template-side: mRNA tail on the forward strand → R1 sees 3' poly-A, R2 sees 5' poly-T in reverse-complement), wrong for poly-G (sequencer-side, hits 3' of both reads).

Net effect of the bug: R2's actual 3' poly-G tail went untrimmed; instead `--poly_g` ate legitimate 5' poly-C content on R2.

## Behaviour change

- ✅ R2 records with 3' poly-G tails are **now trimmed** (previously untouched — this was the bug)
- ✅ R2 records with legitimate 5' poly-C content are **no longer eaten** by \`--poly_g\` (this was the buggy side-effect)
- ✅ R1 / single-end behaviour: **unchanged** (only the R2 path differed)
- ✅ \`--poly_a\` / poly-T behaviour: **unchanged** (still template-side, still cross-strand on R2 — correct as it was)
- ✅ v0.6.x Perl byte-identity: **unaffected** (\`--poly_g\` is a v2.x-only feature; confirmed via \`git show 0.6.11:trim_galore | grep poly_g\` → zero matches)

## Files changed

- \`src/trimmer.rs\` — fix the poly-G branch (drop the \`revcomp = is_r2\` line; always trim 3'); + 3 new lib regression tests
- \`src/main.rs\` — paired summary lines: "R2 reads with poly-C trimmed" → "poly-G"
- \`src/report.rs\` — \`TrimStats\` field docs + report-header text
- \`README.md\` — feature bullet rewritten
- \`docs/src/content/docs/modes/poly.md\` — dedicated prose updated to reflect 3'-both-reads + the why
- \`CHANGELOG.md\` — fix entry under Unreleased

items.title: feat(ui): add files treemap, and the WASM crate's first tests
items.body:
## Summary

Adds `GET /api/files` and a `FilesSection` rendering an SVG treemap — area ∝ lines, fill by health band. Closes #261.

It answers what the ranked tables can't: **where the mass of the codebase sits, and whether the big parts are healthy.** A "10 worst files" table hides one large mediocre file behind ten small terrible ones.

## I scoped my own issue wrong

#261 said *"frontend only, over existing endpoints."* That was incorrect: `/api/health` returns only the **worst 15** files (`WORST_FILES_LIMIT`), and nothing exposed per-file lines for the whole repo. A whole-repo treemap needs a whole-repo endpoint, so this adds one.

## Layout

Hand-written [squarified treemap](https://www.win.tue.nl/~vanwijk/stm.pdf), ~60 lines. Two deliberate calls:

- **No charting dependency.** A WASM binary shouldn't grow one for an algorithm this size.
- **Not slice-and-dice.** It degenerates into unreadable slivers well before this repo's 85 files, and legible area comparison is the entire point of the view.

The layout is pure and deterministic, so the view doesn't reshuffle between loads — the server sorts files largest-first and the tiles follow.

## `unscored` is its own band

`score` is `Option<f64>` end to end rather than defaulting to `10.0`. **A file with no health score is not a healthy file** — coloring unknown risk green would be worse than not coloring it at all. There's a test pinning that `unscored` and `good` never share a fill.

Two related decisions:
- **Color is not the only channel.** Every tile names its band in an SVG `<title>`, and the legend names the bands rather than only showing swatches.
- **`health_available: false` degrades honestly** — sized-but-uncolored tiles *with a stated reason*, not a silently grey blob.

## The WASM crate had no tests — it turns out it could have

While looking for somewhere to test the layout I found the crate **compiles fine for the host target**. Its pure logic was always testable; it simply never was. So this adds 8 tests and a `Test (WASM web crate)` CI step alongside the fmt/clippy steps from #256:

| Property | Why it matters |
| --- | --- |
| Tile areas sum to the canvas | If they don't, the treemap is lying about proportion |
| Area ∝ value | The one thing the view claims |
| Tiles stay in bounds | Silent overflow would clip files out of view |
| Deterministic | No reshuffling between loads |
| Degenerate inputs (empty, zeros, zero-size canvas) | No panics |
| Band boundaries + `unscored` ≠ `good` | The distinction above |

items.body:
Closes #11

## Summary
Adds a new `stripDecorative` option (default: `true`) that removes visually
decorative separator lines (e.g. `-------`, `=======`, `***`) and collapses
3+ consecutive blank lines into one. Zone-aware via the existing
`extractZones` masking strategy, so code blocks, inline code, and markdown
tables are never affected.

## Changes
- New `utils/stripDecorative.ts` — line-filtering transform with zone masking
- New `utils/collapseBlankLines.ts` — shared helper extracted from
  `trimExtraSpaces` to avoid duplicating blank-line collapsing logic
- `types.ts` / `index.ts` — new `stripDecorative` option wired into the
  pipeline (runs after `removeArticles`, before `trimExtraSpaces`)
- `docs/strip-decorative.md` — full before/after examples and edge case table
- README — new options table row, links to the dedicated doc page

## Bugfix (found during implementation)
`extractZones` had a boundary bug where the newline immediately following a
fenced code block's closing fence, or a markdown table's final row, was
incorrectly absorbed into the protected zone's content instead of staying
with the surrounding prose. This was invisible to `trimExtraSpaces` and
`removeArticles` (neither depends on exact line boundaries at zone edges)
but caused an extra blank line to appear when `stripDecorative` split text
by line. Fixed in `findFencedBlock` and `findTable`.

## Testing
Migrated `test/test.ts` to Vitest (`test/test.spec.ts`) for better isolation
and reporting as the suite grows. All 32 tests pass, including 15 new tests
covering: decorator detection for each character type, short-decorator
rejection (`--`), blank-line collapsing, zone interaction with code blocks
and tables, and the `stripDecorative: false` opt-out.

## Version note
`package.json` was out of sync with the published `1.1.0` release (showed
`1.0.1`); synced as part of this branch before the next version bump.

items.body:
## Summary

A Stage-A documentation accuracy sweep was run against the source. Every claim below was traced to the code, config or command it documents; nothing here changes behaviour.

**`README.md` — "Where your data is stored" was wrong for macOS.** The section stated that on "Linux and macOS these stay next to the game". `Config.getUserDataDirectory()` returns `~/Library/Application Support/Roam` when `sys.platform == "darwin"`, and `Config.getSavesBaseDirectory()` resolves saves under it — so the macOS half was incorrect, and it contradicted README's own macOS packaging section a few paragraphs earlier ("User data … is kept under `~/Library/Application Support/Roam`"). It has been replaced by a per-platform table traced against `getUserDataDirectory()`, `getSavesBaseDirectory()` and `screenshotHelper.getScreenshotsFolder()`.

**`README.md` — `ROAM_SAVE_DIR` was undocumented.** `getSavesBaseDirectory()` honours it ahead of every other rule, including `pathToSaveDirectory`. It is now documented alongside the config key.

**`README.md` — the browser frontend had no coverage at all.** A `Dockerfile`, `web/serve.py`, `web/build_zip.py` and `deploy/` configs all ship in the repository, yet no README section described how to run the game in a browser. A "Play in a Browser (from source)" section now documents the Pyodide path, including why `python -m http.server` cannot substitute for `web/serve.py` (the page allocates a `SharedArrayBuffer`, so the COOP/COEP headers sent by `serve.py`'s `end_headers` override are mandatory) and that browser saves live in the browser's own `roam-saves` IndexedDB database.

**`README.md` — the install steps were redundant.** Step 4 (`pip install pygame --pre`) predates the un-pinning of `requirements.txt`, which now specifies `pygame>=2.6.1` and installs it as part of the following step. The two were folded into one and subsequent steps renumbered.

**`LOGGING.md` — "two environment variables" above a three-row table.** `LOG_LEVEL`, `LOG_FORMAT` and `LOG_FILE` are all read by `src/gameLogging/logger.py`.

## Verified clean, deliberately unchanged

- README's Controls table against every entry in `keyBindings.DEFAULT_BINDINGS`
- `PLANNING.md`'s recipe list against `RecipeRegistry`, room types against `RoomType`, mobs against `livingEntityRegistry`
- Every `config.yml` key against its read in `Config.__init__`
- `schemas/goals.json` against `GoalsJsonReaderWriter`
- `docs/roamscript.md` against `tests/integration/`

## Defects found during the sweep, filed rather than fixed

Per the sweep rule that a documentation pass must not silently change code:

- **#550** — `python src/roam.py --web` is broken end to end. `_startHttpServer` rewrites `const WS_PORT = 8765;` into `web/index.html`, but that string (and any `WebSocket` client) no longer exists there, so the WebSocket server has no client; the Pyodide page it serves instead is sent without COOP/COEP, so its `SharedArrayBuffer` allocation cannot succeed; and `--web` never runs `build_zip.py`, so `/web/game.zip` 404s on a fresh clone. `deploy/systemd/roam-web.service` still points at this path while the `Dockerfile` uses `web/serve.py`. This is why the new README section documents the `web/serve.py` path **only**.
- **#551** — both agent-loaded instruction files have drifted from the source tree. Editing agent-loaded config requires separate human authorization and `.github/copilot-instructions.md` is on the do-not-auto-merge path list, so the drift was surfaced rather than edited.

| #415, #416 | Explicitly gated on #393/#396 shipping first |
| #234 | Delegating spatial mechanics to Viron needs a live external Viron server, which is not running here |

items.title: feat: require global args when they cannot be undefined
items.body:
## Problem

Task functions and the resolve result declare the global arguments as `TGlobalArgs`, but the constructor accepted no value at all (`globalArgs?: TGlobalArgs`). So this type checked while handing every task `undefined`:

```ts
new Resolver<{ apiKey: string }>().register({
  id: 'A',
  fn: (_args, globalArgs) => globalArgs.apiKey, // typed { apiKey: string }, actually undefined
});
```

The first property access fails at runtime with no warning from the compiler. The README's "set the arguments later with `setGlobalArgs()`" guidance actively taught this shape, and the `setGlobalArgs` JSDoc example used it too.

## Fix

The constructor now takes a conditional parameter tuple, so the argument is required exactly when `TGlobalArgs` cannot be `undefined`:

```ts
constructor(...args: undefined extends TGlobalArgs ? [globalArgs?: TGlobalArgs] : [globalArgs: TGlobalArgs]) {
  this.globalArgs = (args as [TGlobalArgs?])[0];
}
```

| Usage | `TGlobalArgs` | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `new Resolver()` | `unknown` (default) | optional, still allowed |
| `new Resolver('hello')` | `string` | provided |
| `new Resolver<string \| undefined>()` | admits `undefined` | optional |
| `new Resolver<{ apiKey: string }>({ apiKey })` | required, provided | allowed |
| `new Resolver<{ apiKey: string }>()` | required, missing | **compile error** |

Deferred global arguments are expressed as `Resolver<T | undefined>`, where task functions have to narrow before use.

This is a **type level change only** — the runtime behaviour is unchanged. The single executable difference is the parameter property becoming an explicit assignment.

## Trade-off worth reviewing

Someone who supplies global arguments exclusively through `resolve({ globalArgs })` is now forced to pass a constructor value anyway, or widen the type to `| undefined` and narrow in every task.

`tests/resolver.bench.ts` is exactly that user: it constructed `new Resolver<number>()` and supplied `resolve({ globalArgs: 10 })`, so it was type-unsound but runtime-correct. It is updated to `new Resolver<number>(0)`, where the value is unused because the `resolve()` override wins.

If that pattern deserves better support, the alternative is to leave the constructor as is and accept the unsoundness, or to treat `resolve({ globalArgs })` as a first-class supply path with its own typing. Happy to change direction here.

## Other changes

- `setGlobalArgs` JSDoc — its example used the unsound pattern; now uses `Resolver<T | undefined>` with narrowing.
- **README, Type Safety example** — it passed the *result* shape as the first generic (`TGlobalArgs`), which was incorrect independently of this change. Task result types are inferred from `.register()`, so the example is now `new Resolver()`, matching the surrounding prose.
- **README, Global Arguments** — new subsection covering which constructor forms are allowed and the `| undefined` pattern for deferred arguments.

## Tests

`tests/resolver.interface.type-spec.ts` pins all six cases from the table above. Both `@ts-expect-error` directives were confirmed load-bearing: reverting the source change turns them into `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`.

## Verification

- `vitest run --project node` — 38/38
- `tsc --noEmit` on both the test and examples projects
- `eslint`, `prettier --check`

The browser project could not be run in my environment (the preinstalled Chromium build does not match the pinned `playwright` version), so CI is the first execution of that half.

A `minor` changeset is included, since this breaks compilation for the previously accepted unsound pattern.

## Summary

Parallel counterpart to `knowledge-engine-core` PR #213 (M58's Evidence Intelligence compute layer/CLI), per the project owner's decision to build CLI and web together in the same milestone.

Adds `knowledge_engine_web/evidence_intelligence.py`: a deterministic, no-LLM computation of Evidence Quality, Evidence Consensus, Claim Confidence, and Evidence Coverage, independently rebuilding `knowledge-engine-core`'s `docs/evidence_intelligence_design.md` formula against this project's own `EvidenceRecordDetail`/`RelationshipEdge` dataclasses -- never imports `knowledge_engine`, the same "read `core`'s data, never its code" posture `graph_reader.py`/`report_renderer.py` already follow.

Wires it into `GET /claims/{evidence_record_id}`, right below the existing Evidence Record section, gated on the same `KE_WEB_EVIDENCE_RECORDS_PATH` configuration. The three confidence numbers always render as three separate fields (a table row each), never collapsed into one, and both the HTML table and the plain-text synthesis line trace every number back to a stored field.

**Documentation boundary revision:** `docs/web_design.md`'s Out of Scope section previously stated "Any confidence rating, synthesis, or judgment... Still true, and not open for revision here." This PR revises that explicitly -- documented as a location change (the computation is still fully deterministic, still reads only already-stored fields, still never an LLM or an invented number), not a loosening of the seam. `README.md`'s Seam section is updated to match, and both point to `core_interface_contract.md`'s own matching "Revised in M58" note.

**Live-verified**, not just unit-tested: started a dev server pointed at `core`'s real local database/corpus (the STEP 5 trial claim, which now has 4 real relationship edges after `core`'s M56/M59) and screenshotted the rendered page. This caught a real bug -- see below.

The rendered page showed "Evidence Consensus: 100/100 (3 of 4 agree)" for a claim with 3 `supports` edges and 1 `contextualizes` edge. ## Context

This PR adds back the legacy_deletions CTE to the airbyte_entity_version model to correctly identify and mark entities that were deleted in the legacy dfe-analytics event-stream tables (i.e. before the cutoff timestamp).

The legacy event-stream model has no deleted_at column. An entity deleted in the legacy model can be identified by the fact that all of its versions are closed (no NULL valid_to) and the MAX(valid_to) represents when it was last seen. - Updated `deletions` CTE: on a full-refresh legacy build, UNION ALLs legacy_deletions into the standard deletions channel so pre-cutoff deletions flow through the same downstream logic.

items.title: fix(packaging): fix %%i escaping in shipped systemd user unit and verify in CI
items.body:
## Closes

Closes #44

## Problem

The Debian and RPM packages ship a broken systemd **user** service template at
`/usr/lib/systemd/user/onecloudriver@.service`. The generated unit contains
`%%i` instead of `%i`:

```ini
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/onecloudriver mount /home/%%i/OneDrive -a %%i
```

In systemd unit files `%%` is the escape sequence for a **literal** percent
sign (see `systemd.unit(5)`); only a single `%i` is the instance specifier.
Because the unit contains `%%i`, systemd passes the literal string `%i` to
the command: the account becomes the literal `%i` and the instance
placeholder never expands, so the template unit can never mount for a real
account.

### Root cause

The `Makefile` `SERVICE_UNIT` variable used `%%%%i` (4 percent signs). The
escaping chain is Make → shell → `printf '$(SERVICE_UNIT)'` → unit file.
`printf` collapses `%%` → `%`, so `%%%%i` ended up as `%%i` in the file. To
end up with a single `%i` in the unit file, the variable must contain `%%i`.
The comment above the variable was also incorrect.

The same `SERVICE_UNIT` template is shared by the `deb` and `rpm` targets, so
both packages were affected.

## Solution

- **`Makefile`** — `SERVICE_UNIT` now uses `%%i` (collapses to `%i`) and the
  default mountpoint is `%h/OneDrive/%i` (`%h` = user home, consistent with
  the `service install` fallback `~/OneDrive/%i`). The comment now documents
  the real escaping rule (specifiers are written DOUBLED because `printf`
  collapses `%%` → `%`; a single `%h`/`%i` would be rejected/mangled by
  `printf`).
- **`Makefile`** — the `deb` and `rpm` targets now run a sanity check after
  writing the unit: it fails if `%%i` is present, requires a single `%i`, and
  runs `systemd-analyze verify` when available.
- **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** — new "Verify packaged systemd unit"
  step that extracts the unit from the **actual built packages**
  (`dpkg-deb --fsys-tarfile | tar -xO` for the .deb, `rpm2cpio | cpio` for
  the .rpm) and fails on a leftover `%%i`, so a regression in the packaging
  chain cannot slip through.
- **Docs** — `docs/MANUAL.md`, `docs/MANUAL.es.md`: new section "The packaged
  service unit (deb/rpm)" documenting the shipped template, the `%i`/`%h`
  specifier semantics, how to enable an instance
  (`systemctl --user enable --now 'onecloudriver@user@outlook.com.service'`),
  and that a user-level unit from `service install` takes precedence.
  `README.md` / `README.es.md`: install sections now mention the shipped unit
  and how to enable it.

## Files involved

- `Makefile` — `SERVICE_UNIT` escaping (`%%%%i` → `%%i`), mountpoint
  `%h/OneDrive/%i`, corrected comment, sanity checks in `deb`/`rpm`
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — packaged-unit verification step
- `docs/MANUAL.md`, `docs/MANUAL.es.md` — packaged unit section
- `README.md`, `README.es.md` — install notes for the shipped unit

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./cmd/onecloudriver/... -count=1 -short`
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...`
- [x] Generated unit check: `printf '$(SERVICE_UNIT)'` → single `%i`/`%h`,
      zero `%%i`
- [x] Manual (Debian bookworm container, Go 1.25.12): `make deb` full run →
      unit inside the .deb is
      `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/onecloudriver mount %h/OneDrive/%i -a %i`
      (no `%%i`), `systemd-analyze verify` exit 0

I don't know if the nixos-artwork stuff is retired / deprecated (since the repository is archived), but I made this change for myself, so I figured I'd try contributing it either way.

The [nixos-artwork wallpapers](https://github.com/NixOS/nixos-artwork/tree/master/wallpapers) have derivations in nixpkgs, which includes setting up the directory structures expected by both GNOME and KDE Plasma. However, the metadata is only created using Plasma 5's `metadata.desktop` standard. With Plasma 6, KDE changed the way the metadata needs to be specified, requiring a `metadata.json` file, and expecting the image names to match their resolutions (for multi-resolution support). This PR adds the expected files to the wallpaper derivations so that they are recognized by KDE Plasma 6.

I kept the Plasma 5 metadata in the derivations, in case they are still required for some reason (namely, for anything that consumes the `passthru.kdeFilePath` value). However, we could also consider removing the Plasma 5 support, as I don't believe Plasma 5 is included in nixpkgs at this point. Let me know if you want me to add that change to this PR (otherwise it can be left for its own PR, to keep this PR backport-friendly).

I also made one other unrelated change I discovered while making the Plasma 6 changes, which is fixing the `pname` value for `simple-dark-gray-bottom`. This was incorrectly set to `"simple-dark-gray"`, conflicting with another wallpaper's `pname`, which caused issues with derivation building. I simply set the `pname` value to match the wallpaper name to correct for this.

items.title: Build/docker compose postgres
items.body:
## Summary

Adds local development infrastructure (Docker Compose with PostgreSQL) to
verify the backend against a real database engine, replacing the H2
in-memory database used so far for automated tests. While doing this manual,
end-to-end verification, several real bugs and missing pieces were found in
the REST API layer and fixed in the same branch.

## Why

All previous work (domain model, repositories, reservation service, REST API)
was tested against H2 in-memory. That's fast for automated tests, but doesn't
guarantee the JPA schema and API behavior hold up against real PostgreSQL.
This branch sets up a local Postgres container and manually exercises every
endpoint via Insomnia, which surfaced issues that unit/integration tests with
H2 hadn't caught.

## Infrastructure changes

- `docker-compose.yml` with a `postgres:16` service (persistent volume,
  credentials via `.env`, `.env.example` committed as a template).
- `application-dev.yml` pointing the backend datasource to the local
  container, with `spring.jpa.hibernate.ddl-auto=update` explicitly marked as
  a temporary measure (to be replaced by Flyway once the schema stabilizes).
- Fixed `application.properties`, which had YAML content mistakenly pasted
  into a `.properties` file (leftover duplication, unrelated to Docker).
- `docker/README.md` documenting the local setup.

## Fixes and features found during manual testing

- **Equipment creation no longer requires a `status` field.** A newly created
  equipment item now always starts as `CATALOGUED` automatically, set by the
  server — the client was incorrectly required to supply it.
- **Duplicate equipment names are now rejected (409 Conflict)** instead of
  silently creating duplicates. Restocking existing equipment is now a
  separate, explicit operation.
- **New endpoint** `PATCH /api/equipment/{id}/stock` to replenish stock,
  implemented as an atomic database-level increment to avoid a lost-update
  race condition (simpler than the pessimistic locking used in the
  reservation service, since this is a plain increment rather than a
  check-then-write against a business rule).
- **New nested endpoints** for managing performances within an event
  (`POST` / `GET` / `DELETE /api/events/{eventId}/performances`), which had
  been missed entirely in the initial REST layer. This also restores a
  business rule from the original implementation that had not been migrated
  yet: rejecting exact-duplicate performances (same name, start time,
  duration, and rehearsal time) within the same event.

## Verified manually (Insomnia)

- Equipment: creation, duplicate rejection, stock replenishment, validation
  errors.
- Events: creation, retrieval with nested performances.
- Reservations: the core overlap + stock rule, including the open-interval
  boundary case (an event starting exactly when another ends does not count
  as overlapping).
- Performances: creation, duplicate rejection, listing, deletion — including
  the edge case of deleting a performance ID that belongs to a different
  event (correctly returns 404).

## Deferred to future branches

- Spring Security / authentication and role-based authorization (e.g. only
  administrators should create equipment or users).
- Versioned schema migrations (Flyway), replacing `ddl-auto=update`.
- Logistical feasibility for reservations (teardown + travel time between
  consecutive events).

## How to test

1. `cp docker/.env.example docker/.env`, then `docker compose up -d` from `docker/`.
2. `mvn -f backend/pom.xml spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=dev`
3. Exercise the endpoints (an Insomnia collection covering all the cases
   above is available locally).

items.title: Fix Omie API contract violations in 7 tools (0.2.3)
items.body:
## Summary

This release fixes critical API contract violations in the mcp-omie server that prevented 7 of 30 tools from functioning. Two tools called non-existent Omie API methods, and five sent payloads with incorrect structure and field names. All affected tools have been rewritten to match the official Omie API documentation.

## Key Changes

### Breaking Changes (API contract fixes)

- **`create_order`**: Restructured from flat schema (`codigo_cliente`, `itens`, `data_previsao`) to nested blocks (`cabecalho`, `det[]`, `informacoes_adicionais`). Added required fields `etapa` and `codigo_parcela` to header; moved unit price to `det[].produto.valor_unitario`.

- **`create_service_order`**: Converted from snake_case flat schema to PascalCase nested blocks (`Cabecalho`, `ServicosPrestados[]`, `InformacoesAdicionais`). Field names now match Omie's documented contract (e.g., `cCodIntOS`, `nCodCli`, `nValUnit`).

- **`create_purchase_order`**: Fixed method name from non-existent `IncluirPedidoCompra` to `IncluirPedCompra`. Restructured payload to `cabecalho_incluir` + `produtos_incluir[]` with abbreviated field names (`nCodFor`, `nQtde`, `nValUnit`).

- **`list_purchase_orders`**: Fixed method name from non-existent `ListarPedidosCompra` to `PesquisarPedCompra`. Updated filter structure to use boolean flags (`lExibirPedidos*`) instead of `etapa` enum.

- **`create_stock_adjustment`**: Renamed all fields to match Omie's abbreviated contract (`id_prod`, `quan`, `data`, `tipo`, `origem`, `motivo`, `obs`). Added required `origem` field and exposed `codigo_local_estoque_destino` for transfers.

- **`create_cash_entry`**: Moved `cCodIntLanc` to top level (was incorrectly nested in `cabecalho`). Corrected field structure to match `lanccIncluirRequest` type.

- **`create_invoice`**: Fixed query parameter from non-existent `nIdNF` to `nCodNF` (primary key). Added alternative lookup methods (`nNF` + `serie`, `cChaveNFe`, `nIdPedido`, `cnpj_cpf`).

### Validation & Testing

- Added input validation that checks required fields and basic structure before sending to Omie, providing local error messages for missing mandatory fields.

- Expanded test suite from 53 lines to comprehensive contract verification:
  - Table-driven test covering all 30 tools' `(path, call)` pairs
  - Verification of `param` shape for the 7 rewritten tools
  - Validation tests confirming old field names are no longer sent

### Documentation

- Added `API-AUDIT.md`: detailed audit of all 30 tools against official Omie API reference, documenting status, issues, and recommendations for remaining work.

- Updated `README.md` with breaking change table and migration guide for users upgrading from 0.2.2.

### Version Bump

- Updated version to 0.2.3 in `package.json` and `server.json`.

## Implementation Details

- Schemas now precisely mirror Omie's documented request types, including nested object structures and field naming conventions (snake_case for sales/purchase, PascalCase for services).

- Required fields are now explicitly declared in schemas (e.g., `etapa`, `codigo_parcela` for orders; `origen`, `motivo` for adjustments).

- Test fixtures (`MIN_ARGS`) provide minimal valid arguments for each tool to reach the API layer, enabling contract verification without mocking Omie responses.

- Backward compatibility: old field names are no longer accepted; users must update integration code to use the corrected schemas.

items.body:
## Summary

Clarify that the opt-in protected package-tag profile requires PR-mediated release intent and an authorized maintainer's explicit protected merge, but does not impose an organization-wide independent second-person approval. Repositories without a qualified reviewer should not manufacture a rubber-stamp gate that adds latency without assurance.

Boundary classification: unreleased — corrected in place.

## Scope & non-goals

Included: the central contribution wording, Release and Versioning Standard `2026.08.3`, protected-package-tag profile, ADR-0023, schema/checker documentation, and a new 2026-08-13 validation record.

Not included: schema/checker compatibility changes, approval API automation, Core or Platform edits, GitHub ruleset mutations, release intents, tags, package publication, credentials, or Design System behavior.

## Type of change

- [ ] ✨ Feature (`feat`)
- [ ] 🐛 Fix (`fix`)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (`refactor`)
- [ ] ⚡ Performance (`perf`)
- [ ] 🧹 Chore / build / tooling (`chore`)
- [x] 📝 Docs (`docs`)
- [ ] ✅ Tests (`test`)

## What changed

- Defined reviewable, PR-mediated, authorized, and independently approved as distinct terms.
- Made explicit maintainer merge after repository-required checks the minimum authorization; author and merger may be the same identity.
- Declared `required_approving_review_count: 0` and `require_last_push_approval: false` conformant when PR-only/no-bypass/check invariants remain.
- Preserved exact merge-diff admission, source binding, allowed-path and sibling isolation, immutable tag/registry pairing, fail-closed recovery, deterministic validation, and least-privilege credentials.
- Recorded current Core hosting evidence and current Design System non-selection without mutating either repository.
- Clarified that the dependency-free checker intentionally does not inspect PR approvals; hosting owns the PR-only merge boundary and publication revalidates every prerequisite.

## Key decisions

Mandatory second-person approval was incorrect as a central default because some selecting repositories do not have a qualified independent reviewer or real two-person operating model. An uninformed approval would add delay while producing no meaningful assurance.

Release safety remains the composition of explicit maintainer merge + exact merge-diff admission + repository-required checks + protected package tag + isolated publication credentials. Repositories may still require qualified independent approval when actual reviewer capacity, risk, audit, regulatory, or contractual evidence justifies it.

The schema and checker remain `v1`: neither currently encodes approval identity or count, so no compatibility version or migration is needed.

## Verification

- [x] Lint / format / type checks pass
- [x] Tests pass; unchanged admission behavior has deterministic coverage
- [x] Build / production image succeeds (N/A; no build artifact changed)

## Downstream follow-up

- Core: decide whether to retain optional two-person approval or reconcile active ruleset `20768784` to zero approvals/no last-push approval; in either case preserve PR-only/no-bypass authorization, establish or preserve exact repository-required checks, update ambiguous canonical wording, and keep the missing package-tag ruleset as a fail-closed publication gate.
- Platform: align the few package-boundary uses of “reviewed” with PR-mediated terminology. This is canonical wording reconciliation only; no runtime or hosting change is implied.

items.title: Fix LCD display state machine: separate language from content
items.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes three fundamental confusions in the LCD display state machine (`lineScreenCycle.ts`) where language and content were incorrectly conflated, causing incorrect information to be displayed at wrong times.

## Key Changes

### 1. **Separate exit plan compositions from language** (`lineScreenCycle.ts`, `lineScreen.ts`)
   - Replaced `approachJP`/`approachEN` states with semantic `exitTransfers` and `exitDoors` states
   - `exitTransfers`: Shows station exit plan with transfer lines below (during cruise, under 次は)
   - `exitDoors`: Shows station exit plan with door opening side below (at approach, under まもなく)
   - Removed language parameter from exit plan drawing functions—content is determined by journey phase, not language
   - **Impact**: English-speaking passengers now see which door opens; Japanese passengers no longer see door info 10 stations early

### 2. **Fix station name display** (`lineScreen.ts`)
   - Changed bandeau to display station names in kanji (official names) under all three states: ただいま / 次は / まもなく
   - Previously displayed hiragana (reading) for "next" state (つぎは かんだ), which was incorrect
   - Hiragana readings remain in data (`st.kana`) for platform signage and voice synthesis, not LCD display
   - Updated bandeau label from つぎは to 次は (kanji, matching E235 hardware)

### 3. **Fix campaign notice rotation** (`lineScreenCycle.ts`)
   - Moved security notices, priority seating, and manner mode from global rotation to segment-based system
   - Created `NOTICE_SECTORS` table mapping stations to applicable notices
   - Implemented `segmentKey()` and `segmentNotices()` to determine which notices apply to current segment
   - Notices now appear only on relevant segments (e.g., around Ōsaki, Shinagawa) instead of cycling through every segment
   - **Impact**: Eliminates false repetition of campaign messages 30 times per loop

### 4. **Simplify brake/dwell phase logic** (`lineScreenCycle.ts`)
   - Brake phase now shows only `exitDoors` (no alternation with transfers)
   - Dwell phase shows only line maps (no forced screen at end of stop)
   - Removed `CLOSE_ANNOUNCE_LEAD` logic that was forcing screens to fill gaps

### 5. **Add comprehensive test coverage** (`tests/lineScreenStates.test.ts`)
   - Tests verify language/content separation
   - Tests confirm door info only appears at approach
   - Tests validate station name kanji display
   - Tests ensure campaign notices are segment-based, not rotated globally

## Implementation Details

- **Segment key design**: Uses sorted station codes (`JY09-JY12`) to ensure identical keys regardless of travel direction, preventing accidental single-direction notice registration
- **Deterministic notices**: Segment notices are pre-computed once, not randomly selected per frame, preventing flickering
- **Animated states**: Extracted `ANIMATED_STATES` and `COUNTDOWN_STATES` sets for cleaner state checking
- **LCD probe updates**: Updated test HTML to reflect new state names and show both door-side variants

## Files Modified

- `src/three/lineScreenCycle.ts`: State machine logic, segment notice system
- `src/three/lineScreen.ts`: Drawing functions, station name display, bandeau labels
- `tests/lineScreenStates.test.ts`: New comprehensive test suite
- `lcd-probe.html`: Updated test views to match new state names
- `README.md`: Updated documentation

items.title: feat(bench): add benchmark harness with capacity-invariant regression tests
items.body:
## Intent

The developer asked the agent to add regression tests pinning a previously-fixed bug in the bench package's checkCapacityInvariant function, which had been changed from a pairwise interval-overlap check to a start-point sweep because the old approach false-positived when jobs legitimately bin-pack within a worker's capacity. They required three specific unit tests operating directly on hand-constructed decision logs/intervals (not full scenario runs): (1) bin-packing within capacity — three 1-CPU jobs on a 3-CPU worker should show no violation, and this case should fail under the old pairwise checker but pass under the current one; (2) bin-packing over capacity — a fourth concurrent job pushing combined needs above capacity should be flagged as a violation; (3) an adjacent-interval boundary case where one job ends at tick T and another starts at T with combined needs exceeding capacity, which should show no violation since the check is half-open (t < end). The developer explicitly instructed not to change the checker itself unless a test revealed it was actually incorrect, and asked for confirmation that tests 1 and 3 would fail against a pairwise-overlap implementation and pass against the current sweep implementation.</summary>
</invoke>

- Add the `bench/` package: harness, runner, scenario, workload, metrics, invariants, and report types implementing the reference benchmark harness for evaluating scheduling policies.

- Update `docs/build-log.md` and `README.md`, and add an ADR documenting the move to exact percentiles and replay-not-regenerate for benchmark reporting.

✅ Low: The invariants.go sweep-line fix and its three regression tests are correct, match the requested test cases exactly (verified logic for bin-packing within/over capacity and the half-open adjacent boundary), and the accompanying bench harness code is well-scoped, deterministic, and internally consistent; the only issue found is a commit-hygiene mismatch (feature code mislabeled as a docs commit) rather than a functional or correctness defect.

items.title: Separate immutable release provenance from current-main CI
items.body:
## Summary

- separate strict explicit release-candidate validation from immutable tagged-release validation
- validate the recorded annotated tag object and peeled target before accepting post-release descendants
- reconstruct and run the complete suite from an isolated detached worktree at the exact tagged commit
- keep current-main builds and tests distinct from immutable-release reconstruction in CI
- document the post-release provenance policy and exact reconstruction workflow

## Root cause

After `v1.0.0`, a documentation-only commit on `main` was incorrectly treated as though current `HEAD` had to remain the original release candidate. That made current-main CI fail provenance closure even though the annotated tag, tagged tree, audit evidence, and release assets were unchanged.

Explicit `--candidate <sha>` validation remains strict and rejects post-tag descendants. The tagged-release path instead validates the immutable tag object and target, then reports the current descendant separately.

## Scope and validation

The repair changes only CI policy, provenance/reproducibility scripts and tests, and policy/testing documentation. It does not modify `README.md`, C++ product sources, either release, either tag, or any release asset.

Completed local validation includes the full 13-package exact-tag reconstruction suite, Release/ASan/UBSan/TSan builds with all 30 CTest cases in each configuration, provenance and reproducibility regression suites, release metadata/artifact checks, secret/public-history scans, YAML validation, and Python compilation.

items.title: [v0.6.0] Fix two false negatives in the contrast and focus-indicator checks
items.body:
## Summary
- `bg-linear-*`/`bg-conic-*` (Tailwind v4's gradient-angle utilities, e.g. `bg-linear-45`, `bg-conic-180`) share the same `word-NN` shape as a color token in `extractClasses.ts`'s `COLOR_TOKEN` regex. Since class extraction takes the last matching token, `bg-red-500 bg-linear-45` resolved to the gradient utility instead of the real color, failed to resolve, and silently dropped the contrast check for that element — a real WCAG violation reported as zero. Excluded via `NON_COLOR_SCALE_NAMES`, the same fix shape already used for `bg-opacity-50`.
- `checkFocusIndicator.ts`'s `isReplacement()` treated any `bg-*`/`border-*`/`ring-*`/`shadow-*`/`outline-*`-prefixed class as a valid replacement for a removed focus outline. Utilities sharing those prefixes — `bg-fixed`, `bg-repeat`, `bg-clip-text`, `border-collapse`, etc. — control layout/rendering behavior, not a visible color/width/style, so `focus:outline-none focus:bg-fixed` was incorrectly passing as compliant. Added a `NON_VISUAL_BASES` Set (31 entries) + `NON_VISUAL_PATTERN` (`bg-blend-*`), mirroring the existing `DEGENERATE_BASES`/`MODIFIER_ONLY` denylist.
- Also fixes stale docs: a false "not yet published to npm" claim in `packages/tailwind-a11y/CLAUDE.md`, a stale `^0.1.0` dependency-range example in the root `CLAUDE.md`, and two READMEs (`tailwind-a11y`, `vscode-tailwind-a11y`) missing the GitHub Action adapter from their related-packages sections.

## Versions
- `tailwind-a11y`: `0.5.1` → `0.6.0` (MINOR — both fixes increase the set of reported violations; a project relying on either decoy pattern can newly fail CI)
- `eslint-plugin-tailwind-a11y`: dependency range `^0.5.0` → `^0.6.0` (a MINOR engine bump falls outside the old caret range) and its own version synced to `0.6.0` to match the engine
- `vscode-tailwind-a11y`: dependency range bump to `^0.6.0` plus a version sync to `0.6.0` — it bundles the engine, so it needs a rebuild+republish regardless of its own source not changing

items.title: Fix DB migration failures on legacy schemas and admin login
items.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes two critical issues that prevented application startup and login:

1. **STG deployment failure**: `alembic upgrade head` was failing with `Table '...' already exists` when applied to databases with Alembic-untracked tables (legacy schemas from previous baseline SQL operations).
2. **Admin login failure**: The default admin account could not log in with documented credentials (`admin@example.com` / `admin`) because the password hash was incorrectly set to hash of the email address instead of the password.

## Key Changes

### DB Migration Self-Healing (`scripts/run_db_migrations.py`)

- **New script** that wraps `alembic upgrade head` with pre-flight schema detection
- Implements three-way branching strategy:
  - **Fresh DB** (no tables or only `alembic_version` exists): Run `upgrade head` normally
  - **Legacy untracked schema** (all `init_master` tables exist but no `alembic_version`): Auto-stamp to `init_master` baseline, then `upgrade head` (automates the manual procedure from ADR-0001)
  - **Ambiguous partial schema** (some but not all tables exist): Error out and require manual investigation
- Resolves database URL with same priority as `migrations/env.py` (environment variable > `alembic.ini`)
- Resolves `alembic.ini` by absolute path to work from any working directory

### Admin Password Hash Correction

- **Updated `DEFAULT_ADMIN_PASSWORD_HASH`** in `shared/domain/auth/master_data.py` to correct hash of plaintext `"admin"` (was incorrectly hashing `"admin@example.com"`)
- **New migration** `5a6b39ff7ecc_fix_default_admin_password_hash.py`:
  - Corrects existing databases that have the broken hash
  - Respects users who have already changed their password (only updates rows with the legacy broken hash)
  - Supports `ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD` environment variable for custom initial passwords

### Deployment Script Updates

- Updated `scripts/entrypoint.sh` to call `python scripts/run_db_migrations.py` instead of bare `alembic` command
- Updated `scripts/deploy.sh` and `scripts/deploy-stg.sh` to use the new migration script with retry logic
- Removed `-c migrations/alembic.ini` flags (no longer needed with absolute path resolution)

### Documentation & Tests

- **Updated `migrations/README.md`**: Explains the three-way branching logic and when manual `stamp` is needed
- **Updated `scripts/README.md`**: Documents the new wrapper script and its self-healing behavior
- **Updated `docs/CHANGELOG.md`**: Detailed explanation of both fixes and their root causes
- **Unit tests** (`tests/unit/core/test_run_db_migrations.py`): Pure function tests for `decide_strategy()` covering all three branches
- **Integration tests** (`tests/integration/test_db_migrate_self_heal.py`): Full flow tests with SQLite file databases
- **Regression test** (`tests/integration/test_default_admin_login.py`): Verifies admin can log in with documented credentials after all migrations
- **Updated `tests/unit/core/test_alembic_config.py`**: Validates that deployment scripts use the new migration wrapper

## Implementation Details

- The migration script is DB-agnostic for the decision logic (pure function `decide_strategy()` for testability)
- Uses SQLAlchemy inspector to detect existing tables without requiring full model imports
- Loads all model definitions to determine target table set (ensures consistency with current schema)
- Temporarily sets `DATABASE_URI` environment variable during migration to ensure `migrations/env.py` uses the same database URL as the detection phase
- Handles both fresh deployments and legacy schema recovery in a single, deterministic flow

items.body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes two backend contract mismatches that were breaking the Microsoft OAuth login flow and the similar incidents preview in the frontend.

---

## Type of change

- fix — bug fix

---

## Changes made

### Fix 1 — GET /auth/me missing role field
- `authController.js` — added `role: user.roleName` to the `getProfile` response
- Root cause: `getProfile` was written from day one without the `role` field, even though `PostgresUserRepo.findById()` already fetched it via JOIN
- Impact: Microsoft OAuth frontend flow calls `GET /auth/me` to hydrate the user after receiving tokens — without `role`, `navigate(DASHBOARD_ROUTES[user.role])` resolved to `navigate(undefined)` and the user was stuck on the 'Signing in...' spinner forever
- Regular email/password login was unaffected because `POST /auth/login` builds its own response object that always included `role`

### Fix 2 — POST /incidents/similar response key mismatch
- `incidentController.js` — matched the response key to what the frontend expects
- Root cause: backend and frontend were using different field names for the similar incidents list
- Impact: frontend similar incidents preview was broken

### Docs — README updates
- `README.md` (root) — rewritten in English, corrected stack (was incorrectly listing NestJS/Prisma/TypeORM — actual stack is Express + pg + Zod + Winston), added complete endpoint list, real environment URLs, CI/CD workflows
- `backend/README.md` — rewritten in English, added all 48 endpoints grouped by module, complete env vars list, database tables and migrations, testing instructions
- `frontend/README.md` — created from scratch in English, screens by role, state management, Socket.io events, build targets (web/Android/Electron)

---

## How to test

1. Login with Microsoft OAuth → user should land on the correct dashboard (student/manager/admin) instead of looping back to login
2. `GET /api/v1/auth/me` → response now includes `role` field
3. `POST /api/v1/incidents/similar` → response key matches frontend expectation
4. `npm test` → 81/81 unit tests passing
5. `npm run test:integration` → 87 integration tests, requires a reachable local PostgreSQL instance to run

---

## Root cause analysis

`GET /auth/me` never included `role` from day one — not a regression. It was only discovered now because Nayeli updated the Microsoft OAuth callback flow to call `authService.me()` to hydrate the user session, which exposed the missing field. Regular login (`POST /auth/login`) always built its own response with `role` so that flow was never affected.

items.title: Architecture: Establish Strict Ownership Boundaries Between Project and KDSE Runtime
items.body:
## Summary

This PR establishes strict ownership boundaries between the software project and the KDSE runtime, correcting architectural drift where `.kdse/` was incorrectly treated as the project workspace.

## Problem

The current KDSE implementation incorrectly treats `.kdse/` as the project workspace, causing:
- Project documentation created inside `.kdse/`
- Standard software engineering practices ignored
- Runtime artifacts and project artifacts mixed together

## Solution

### Four Ownership Domains

1. **Project Layer** (Owned by Software Project)
   - README.md, LICENSE, docs/, src/, tests/, cmd/, etc.
   - Location: Project root

2. **Runtime Layer** (Owned by KDSE Runtime)
   - runtime/, sessions/, state/, cache/, reports/, evidence/
   - Location: `.kdse/`

3. **Reference Layer** (Owned by KDSE Runtime)
   - External standards (IEC 61850, Modbus, IEEE, etc.)
   - Location: `.kdse/references/`

4. **Knowledge Layer** (Owned by KDSE Runtime)
   - Extracted knowledge from references
   - Location: `.kdse/knowledge/`

## Changes

### Documentation
- `docs/architecture/AUDIT-ARCHITECTURE-DRIFT.md` - Architecture audit documenting the drift
- `docs/architecture/OWNERSHIP_MODEL.md` - Ownership model documentation
- `docs/architecture/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md` - Verification report
- Updated `README.md` with correct philosophy

### Code
- `internal/workspace/engine.go` - Updated initialization to create standard project layout
- `internal/workspace/ownership.go` - New artifact ownership classification module
- `internal/guard/ownership_guard.go` - New ownership enforcement guard

### Migration
- Moved `laboratory/` to `.kdse/laboratory/`
- Moved `runtime/` documentation to `docs/runtime/`

## Core Principle

> **"KDSE augments software engineering, it never replaces it."**

A KDSE-enabled repository must remain a standard software project. Any engineer unfamiliar with KDSE should still be able to understand, build, deploy, and maintain the project without understanding KDSE internals.

## Testing

- Docker build verified successfully

- Initialization creates standard project layout
- Ownership enforcement prevents violations
